title: How to repair a cross-stitch mistake
subtitle: Unpicking stitches cleanly without damaging the fabric or the surrounding work
excerpt: Unpicking cross-stitch is part of the craft. A miscount, a wrong colour, or a stitch worked in the wrong direction can be removed without trace if done carefully. The tools needed are small embroidery scissors, a seam ripper or stiletto, and patience. The fabric and surrounding stitches should be undamaged when done.
sourceNotes: Cross-stitch correction technique. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The weave can be damaged by repeated unpicking in the same area.
The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Once unpicked, the floss is usually too short or kinked to re-use; cut a fresh length.

content.text: Unpicking a mistake in cross-stitch is straightforward if done carefully. Cut the

and pull the short pieces through to the back, rather than trying to pull the whole length back out from the front. This avoids distorting the surrounding stitches and keeps the thread ends manageable.

Work from the back of the fabric whenever possible. Turn the piece over and identify which thread runs correspond to the stitches to be removed. On 14-count Aida the thread runs are visible and easy to trace.

Using small sharp embroidery scissors, snip the thread at the back in the middle of a run, not at the anchor point. Then snip again a few stitches away in the same run. This gives you a short piece to pull out cleanly.

Use a seam ripper or a stiletto (a pointed awl) to lift the cut thread ends from the back of the fabric and pull them through to the back. Work gently; never pull so hard that the tool catches in the Aida weave.
Once the thread is removed, check the fabric from the front. The Aida should be undisturbed, the grid holes clear and round. If any thread fuzz remains in the holes, use the stiletto to lift it out.

Re-stitch the area with a fresh cut length. The new stitches should sit smooth in the same holes as before. If the fabric threads look distorted after unpicking, a light pressing with steam from the back will help restore the weave.

items.symptom: The fabric looks pilled or fuzzy after unpicking
items.cause: The scissors caught the Aida threads rather than just the floss, or the thread was pulled sideways rather than straight through the hole.
items.fix: Always cut on the back and pull straight through, not at an angle. Use the finest scissors you have for close work, and move slowly. If the fabric is already damaged, press from the back with steam to neaten the weave; badly damaged Aida in the design area may need patching.

items.symptom: The surrounding stitches came loose when unpicking
items.cause: The thread for the mistake area was also the anchor run for adjacent stitches.
items.fix: When unpicking one area, check the back first to see if the thread runs connect to surrounding stitches. If they do, cut only within the mistake area and anchor the surrounding stitches with a fresh anchor stitch before removing the mistake thread.

content.text: After unpicking and re-stitching, compare the repaired area with the surrounding work in good light. A careful repair is nearly invisible on cross-stitch because the stitches are regular and small. Mistakes that are caught early unpick more cleanly than those left in for several sessions.
